prerequisites.note: ./gradlew check BUILD SUCCESSFUL (compile + checkstyle + jacoco verification). spec.md present. Flyway V32/V33 compiled.

findings.message: findExpiryCandidateWallets paginates via Pageable but JPQL had no ORDER BY despite the comment claiming 'Order by id for stable paging'. Offset paging without a deterministic sort can skip or double-process candidate wallets across pages.
findings.fixApplied: Added ORDER BY w.id to the @Query.

findings.message: getExpiringSoon used LocalDate.now() (JVM default zone) while the rest of the feature uses LocalDate.now(ZoneOffset.UTC). On a non-UTC server the preview window boundary shifts by a day.

@Data + @EqualsAndHashCode(callSuper=true) generates equals/hashCode over mutable persistent fields, breaking hash-collection semantics across the entity lifecycle. JPA entities should base identity on the immutable id only.
Same @Data/@EqualsAndHashCode anti-pattern over mutable fields (status, notifiedAt, expiredAmount) as the entity moves through SCHEDULED->NOTIFIED->EXPIRED.

@Scheduled runExpirySweep has no distributed lock (no ShedLock). Multi-instance deployments run the sweep concurrently; the warn-phase check-then-act is protected only by the DB unique index, causing duplicate work + noisy ConstraintViolation logs. Expire phase is safe (lock-then-check).

Expire phase loads ALL due NOTIFIED notices for a policy into one List with no pagination, unlike the deliberately-paged warn phase (CANDIDATE_BATCH_SIZE=500, AC-10). A large backlog could load a very large list into heap.
advanceToNotified calls publishAndConfirm which blocks up to 15s for a Kafka ack once per candidate wallet inside the per-page loop. Broker degradation could serialize 15s waits per wallet.
Expire phase re-checks policy.isEnabled() against the policy snapshot loaded at sweep start, not a fresh DB read. A mid-sweep disable committed elsewhere is not visible.
new HashMap<>() in bulkLastActivity sized for a page of known max size (CANDIDATE_BATCH_SIZE=500) — default capacity rehashes while filling.
CSV StringBuilder seeded only with header; grows from default capacity per row. Row count is known up front.
escapeCsv performs four separate full-string contains() scans per cell in the export hot path; a single-pass char scan would suffice. Measure first.
cancellationEvents ArrayList created at default capacity though pending.size() upper bound is known.
isMaterialChange returns false for a new entity but the inline comment says 'treat as material change when enabling'. Behavior is correct; the comment is misleading and invites a wrong future fix.

Warn-phase find-or-create + save runs in auto-commit with no row lock; correctness relies entirely on the DB unique constraint to reject duplicate (wallet, currency, scheduledExpiryDate) inserts under overlapping sweeps.

totalExpiredAmount cell was appended via toPlainString() without CsvUtil.escapeCsv(). A negative BigDecimal renders with a leading '-', one of CsvUtil's formula-injection trigger chars (=+-@\t\r), defeating the CWE-1236 protection applied to every other cell.
findings.fixApplied: Wrapped the numeric cell in CsvUtil.escapeCsv(...). No-op for valid positive amounts; neutralizes the anomalous negative case.

findings.message: findByActorIdAndResourceType is not tenant-scoped (filters only on actorId UUID + resourceType, no clientId). If any caller derives actorId from request input, this permits cross-tenant audit-log reads (OWASP A01).
findings.note: Requires caller analysis; may be an intentional GDPR/admin path. Manual review.

findings.message: anonymizeByActorId is a bulk @Modifying UPDATE keyed only on actorId with no clientId scope. A tenant-unbounded destructive write risks anonymizing other tenants' rows if actorId is attacker-influenced.
findings.note: May be an intentional GDPR cross-tenant erasure path; confirm against spec/callers.

findings.message: handleIllegalArgument returns raw ex.getMessage() to the client as the 400 body, potentially leaking internal detail (enum-parse failures, identifiers). Other handlers return generic messages and keep internals in the log.

inactivityDays has no @Min/@Max bound (leadTimeDays does); fixedExpiryDate has no temporal guard; mode-dependent required fields are not enforced declaratively, deferring all validation to the service.
exportBreakageCsv declares ResponseEntity<Object> (byte[] on 200, ErrorResponse on 429). Untyped Object erases the response contract and blocks accurate OpenAPI schema generation.
PUT /policies/{currencyId} is an upsert that always returns 200, including on first creation; 201 Created would be more correct on create.
getExpiringSoon withinDays is required=false with no defaultValue and no documented fallback; the default lead window is implicit in the service and absent from the contract.

contract-compliance.note: All 5 endpoints in contracts/endpoints/balance-expiration.yaml have matching controller methods (paths, GET/PUT verbs, path/query params, permissions configure/view_breakage, status codes incl. 429). Request DTO matches schema (@NotNull on the 3 required fields). Dedicated BalanceExpirationContractConformanceTest validates responses against the OpenAPI spec.

findings.summary: Company-wallet expiry notifications broadcast to all partner roles
findings.details: For COMPANY wallets resolveRecipients returns an empty targetUserIds list. NotificationDispatcher:60-91 treats an empty target list as a role-broadcast, querying ALL tenant users holding the type's default roles (V33 seeds PARTNER_SELLER + PARTNER_ADMIN). Audience filtering only applies when metadata carries incentiveId, which the balance-expiry events do not. The events carry only walletId in metadata and there is no partnerCompanyId field on NotificationEvent, so a single COMPANY wallet's expiry notifies every partner seller/admin in the tenant. Confidentiality / trust-boundary failure.
findings.tierReason: severity=high, confidence=0.85 (>=0.70), alreadyHandled=false (verified via NotificationDispatcher:60-91 broadcast path + NotificationEvent has no partnerCompanyId)
findings.recommendation: Resolve COMPANY wallet recipients to users scoped to wallet.partnerCompanyId, or extend NotificationEvent/NotificationDispatcher to carry and enforce a partnerCompanyId audience filter before broadcasting.

findings.summary: Inactivity notices are not revalidated before irreversible expiry
findings.details: processExpireForNotice (lines 426-491) locks the wallet, checks idempotency and zero-balance, then debits the full live availableBalance to zero. It never re-checks the latest ledger activity timestamp for INACTIVITY policies — that lookup only happens in the warn phase. A wallet that receives CREDIT/DEBIT/RESERVE/RETURN_CREDIT after the warning but before the scheduled date still gets expired from the stale notice, defeating inactivity semantics and destroying valid balance.
findings.tierReason: severity=high, confidence=0.85 (>=0.70), alreadyHandled=false (verified: expire path has no activity recheck — only policy-enabled, lock, idempotency, zero-balance guards)
findings.recommendation: Inside processExpireForNotice, after locking the wallet, re-fetch max ledger activity for INACTIVITY policies and recompute the expiry date; if the notice is stale, cancel or reschedule instead of debiting. Also consider cancelling/updating pending notices on wallet mutations.

findings.summary: Fixed-date policies can expire immediately after a late first warning
findings.details: Fixed-date validation (BalanceExpirationPolicyService:199-207) only requires fixedExpiryDate to be after today; it does not account for leadTimeDays or the enabled_at grace window. A tenant can enable a fixed-date policy for tomorrow with a 30-day lead time: the warn phase waits until enabled_at + leadTimeDays, creates the first NOTIFIED notice for a date already in the past, and the same sweep can expire the wallet immediately — defeating the advance-warning guarantee.
findings.recommendation: Reject fixed dates that cannot satisfy the configured advance-warning/grace window, or make expiry eligibility depend on notifiedAt + leadTimeDays rather than scheduledExpiryDate alone.

classificationRules.blockingThreshold: severity critical/high AND confidence >= 0.70 AND not alreadyHandled
classificationRules.advisoryThreshold: severity medium/low OR confidence < 0.70 OR alreadyHandled

- [high] Company-wallet expiry notifications broadcast to all partner roles (BalanceExpiryBatchService.java:607-617)
- [high] Inactivity notices are not revalidated before irreversible expiry (BalanceExpiryBatchService.java:383-484)

- Block shipment until expiry execution revalidates activity and notification audience scoping is fixed.
